question.prompt: Positive integers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are chosen so that \(a \lt b \lt c,\) and the system of equations \[2x + y = 2003\] and \[ \begin{aligned} &y = |x - a| + |x - b| \\ &\quad {}+ |x - c| \end{aligned} \] has exactly one solution. What is the minimum value of \(c?\)

solutions.explanation:
Substituting the absolute-value expression for \(y\) into the first equation reduces the system to one equation:
\[
F(x)=2003,
\qquad
F(x)=2x+|x-a|+|x-b|+|x-c|.
\]
Each solution for \(x\) determines exactly one \(y\), so it is enough to count the solutions of this equation. The order \(a<b<c\) tells us where the absolute-value signs change:
\[
F(x)=
\begin{cases}
a+b+c-x,&x\le a,\\
x-a+b+c,&a\le x\le b,\\
3x-a-b+c,&b\le x\le c,\\
5x-a-b-c,&x\ge c.
\end{cases}
\]
The formulas agree at their shared endpoints. Their coefficients of \(x\) are \(-1,1,3,5\), respectively. Thus \(F\) strictly decreases up to \(a\), then strictly increases after \(a\). Its unique minimum is
\[
F(a)=b+c.
\]
The left and right branches both take arbitrarily large values. Consequently, the level \(2003\) gives no solution if \(2003<b+c\), one solution if \(2003=b+c\), and two solutions if \(2003>b+c\), one on each side of \(a\). Exactly one solution therefore requires
\[
b+c=2003.
\]
Since \(b,c\) are integers with \(b<c\), we have \(b\le c-1\), so
\[
2003=b+c\le2c-1,
\qquad c\ge1002.
\]
This bound is attainable with \((a,b,c)=(1,1001,1002)\). The unique solution then occurs at \(x=a=1\), with \(y=2001\), which satisfies both original equations. Hence the minimum is \(\boxed{1002}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Locate the unique minimum of a piecewise linear function
